title: Docs: Hosted data residency enforcement (region pinning) guide + FAQ + error handling examples
author: Wei Chen
description: Adds end-user documentation for Hosted Data Residency Enforcement (region pinning) covering: how to enable/configure at org/project level, runtime behavior and routing guarantees, error codes and remediation (including SDK examples), audit logging evidence, and an FAQ (Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private/VPC). Also adds a short “Support & escalation” section with the expected triage artifacts (request_id, org, pinned/allowed regions, base URL / SDK region config) and links to enterprise packaging guidance. This is intended to ship alongside the residency enforcement rollout gates and error contract standardization (PM-482 / ENG-2842 / ENG-2847).

body: Summary This PR documents Hosted Data Residency Enforcement (aka “region pinning”) for Redwood Inference. The goal is to give enterprise admins and platform engineers a clear, actionable guide for enabling the feature and understanding what happens when a request violates residency policy. What’s included New docs pages: Data residency overview (what’s in-scope, what’s not, supported regions, how guarantees differ by product tier) Enablement & configuration: org/project-level region pinning settings (pinned_region and allowed_regions) including validation rules and common misconfigurations Behavior & enforcement: admission-time enforcement before model execution; deterministic routing behavior when pinned (no cross-region fallback unless explicitly allowed by policy/exception); downstream write behavior for logs/audit events Error handling: standardized error codes and examples, including RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH and RESIDENCY_POLICY_REQUIRED, with remediation steps (update base URL, set SDK region hint, verify org/project policy) Observability & evidence: audit log event types residency.policy_evaluated and residency.violation, example payloads, and SIEM ingestion notes FAQ: Dedicated vs Hosted, Private/VPC semantics, retries, capacity exhaustion behavior, and how exceptions work Support & escalation: what to collect for Support (request_id, timestamp, org/project, pinned/allowed regions, client base URL, SDK version/region hint, and whether allow_cross_region_fallback exception is in place). References Support/Jira drivers: SUP-3921 (EU-only assurance), SUP-3988 (denials when hitting US endpoint after enabling beta), SUP-4077 (sample audit payloads/retention). Rollout context: PM-482. Notes on behavior documented in this PR Region selection: Customers can either (1) use the region-specific base URL (recommended), or (2) provide an SDK region hint; both must align with pinned/allowed region policy. If a customer is pinned to eu-west, requests sent to a us-east endpoint will be denied with a clear error code and a docs link. Fallback: When region pinning is enabled, cross-region fallback is not performed by default; docs call out that any temporary override requires an approved exception and will be recorded via audit events. Private/VPC: Docs clarify that data residency for Private is controlled by customer-managed deployment topology; the “Hosted enforcement” features are not applicable in the same way, but audit events and configuration concepts are referenced for consistency. Example snippets included Example violation response payload includes machine-readable error code, message, and remediation URL. Example curl shows a pinned EU org hitting a US endpoint resulting in RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH. SDK snippets demonstrate catching typed exceptions and logging request_id for Support escalation. Screenshots/UX notes The guide references Console settings labels as of DES-211/ENG-2846; no screenshots included yet (blocked on final copy + feature flag exposure in staging). QA / validation Ran docs build locally (yarn build). Ran markdown lint + link check. Spot-validated error payload examples against latest gateway contract shared by Platform (ENG-2842).
review_conversation: Elliot Price (review): Structure looks good. Can we add a one-paragraph definition up top that explicitly lists “in-scope data” (prompts/completions/embeddings payloads, request metadata, logs, optional persistence) and says enforcement applies to both execution region and downstream writes?
Wei Chen (author): Added “What counts as in-scope data” section to the overview page and referenced it from the FAQ + audit logs page.

Naomi Feldman (review): Please be more explicit that cross-region fallback is disabled when pinned (unless an exception is explicitly granted). Also add a line that violation events are audit logged for compliance evidence.

Wei Chen (author): Updated Behavior section + FAQ “What happens during capacity exhaustion?” to emphasize no cross-region fallback by default; added audit logging note and linked audit log event examples.

Brian Murphy (review): Error examples should match the standard shape (error.code, error.message, error.request_id, error.docs_url). Also avoid calling it “403” unconditionally; we’ve been using 409 for policy conflicts in other places.

Wei Chen (author): Aligned payload shape and removed hard-coded HTTP status where we don’t have final decision; now states “status depends on endpoint; see Errors page” and links to the canonical error codes doc. Left examples with RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH and request_id + docs_url.
Marcus Lin (review): For the audit log examples: make sure we don’t imply we log raw prompt content in audit events. Audit events should reference request_id and policy decision metadata only.
Wei Chen (author): Adjusted wording and example payloads to exclude prompt/completion content; added a note that audit events contain metadata and identifiers, not model inputs/outputs.

Dev Patel (review): Support section: add “SDK version” and “client base URL” to the checklist, and include the two most common causes we’ve seen (wrong endpoint region; project override differs from org pinning).
Wei Chen (author): Added both items + common causes list; linked to support escalation page and included request_id as the primary handle.
release_notes: Documentation: Added Hosted Data Residency Enforcement docs (enablement, behavior, FAQ, audit evidence, and error handling examples).
